name: MAK - Museum of Applied Arts
funding: 2024: EUR 16.1M income, EUR 11.7M of it federal base funding; sponsors Porsche Holding Salzburg, Wienerberger, Wiener Städtische, Swarovski and others.
watch: Porsche Holding Salzburg, a VW Group firm, began a multi-year partnership in 2024; 174,476 visitors in 2024.
records_note: The MAK posts annual reports for 2017 to 2025, audited accounts, a named 2024 sponsor thank-you list and its Kuratorium members.

name: Vitra Design Museum
funding: 2025-26: private foundation subsidised by Vitra AG; show sponsors include Maharam, Camper and IKEA Stiftung, plus the Design Circle friends.
watch: Independent foundation set up by Vitra and Rolf Fehlbaum in 1989; furniture-company money throughout.
records_note: The museum posts no annual reports, accounts, donor list or board; sponsors appear only as credits on individual exhibition pages.

name: Corning Museum of Glass
funding: 2023: US$42.5M revenue, US$25.1M of it contributions; founder Corning Incorporated is the main funder.
watch: Founded 1951 by Corning Glass Works; budget is large but attendance (about 400k, 2012) is under the 500k line.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports from 2010 to 2024, audited statements, a named Business Alliance list and its trustees.

name: Die Neue Sammlung - The Design Museum
funding: 2025: Bavarian state museum; its centenary show was funded by the Bavarian arts ministry and PIN. Freunde, whose corporate partner is Allianz (insurance).
watch: Insurance money (Allianz) reaches it through the PIN. friends' association; no controversy found in English or German.
records_note: This Bavarian state museum posts no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; sponsors appear only as credits on exhibition pages.

name: Japan Folk Crafts Museum (Nihon Mingeikan)
funding: 2025: public-interest foundation chaired by Naoto Fukasawa, run on admissions, members' dues (corporate from JPY 100k) and donations; no roster published.
watch: Founded 1936 by Yanagi Soetsu with backing from industrialist Ohara Magosaburo; supporting members are not named.
records_note: The foundation posts yearly business reports for FY2018 to FY2025, income and expenditure statements and its officer list, but no donor roster.

name: Cheongju Craft Biennale
funding: 2025: city-run (committee chaired by Cheongju's mayor) with national Korea Art Festival support; partners Hyundai Motor, Genesis, Hyundai Department Store, Aero K, Emart24.
watch: Hyundai Motor, a 2025 partner: its subsidiary SMART Alabama hired children as young as 12 (Reuters, 2022). Over 400,000 visitors in 2025.
records_note: Its site failed a certificate check; searches found only press coverage of the organizing committee, no reports, accounts, donors or board.

name: Künstlerhaus Bethanien
funding: Institutional funding comes from the Berlin Senate Department for Culture, cut by about EUR 149k in 2025; national arts councils and KfW Stiftung fund residencies.
watch: Residency house founded 1974. About 30 foreign arts councils and ministries pay for its studio places.
records_note: Bethanien names its partners and funders on one undated page but posts no annual reports, accounts or board; its team page names two directors.

name: Akademie Schloss Solitude
funding: A public-law foundation run and financed by the state of Baden-Württemberg; programme partners include KfW Stiftung and Robert Bosch GmbH.
watch: State-founded residency (1990) in a baroque palace. It runs a code of conduct for fellows, introduced after an Oct 2023 open letter.
records_note: Solitude names its foundation board and trustees, but posts no annual reports, accounts or funder list; project partners are credited on programme pages.

name: Cité internationale des arts
funding: A public-benefit foundation funded by France's Ministry of Culture, the City of Paris and the Académie des Beaux-Arts, plus about 135 partners who rent studios.
watch: 310 live-in studios in the Marais and Montmartre. Corporate patrons are Samsung Foundation of Culture, Icatu and Neuflize OBC.
records_note: The Cité posts annual reports for 2023 to 2025, a named partner list and its board, but no financial statements.

name: Skowhegan School of Painting & Sculpture
funding: About US$4.1M in expenses in 2023 (Form 990), all privately raised: a US$21M+ 75th-anniversary campaign that ended in Feb 2023, an annual gala and foundations.
watch: Summer residency in Maine. Campaign donors include the Kellen, Acquavella, Palm, Pollock-Krasner and Frankenthaler foundations and Agnes Gund.
records_note: Only the 2025 annual report is online, with donors named by giving level; Form 990s are on ProPublica and trustees and governors are listed.

name: Cove Park
funding: Income was GBP 611k in FY2025 (OSCR); funders are Creative Scotland multi-year funding plus GBP 286k Culture Collective money (2026), trusts and individuals.
watch: Rural residency on Loch Long, founded in 1999 by Eileen and Peter Jacobs. Creative Scotland has funded it regularly since 2018.
records_note: Cove Park names its funders (dated 2 April 2026) and trustees and files full accounts at Companies House, but posts no annual reports.

name: Art-Belarus Gallery (Belgazprombank corporate collection)
watch: Gallery at the Palace of Arts, Kozlova 3, built around the bank's Paris School collection (Chagall, Soutine, Kikoine) started 2011–12; the project site is still live (2014–2026) and claims 20 exhibitions in 8 cities and 300,000+ visitors.
why_flagged: Gallery at the Palace of Arts, Kozlova 3, built around the bank's Paris School collection (Chagall, Soutine, Kikoine) started 2011–12; the project site is still live (2014–2026) and claims 20 exhibitions in 8 cities and 300,000+ visitors.
records_note: The gallery's site returned only a verification page, so none of the four questions could be checked and no register was reachable.
